s.note: Pizza dough scrolls with tomato, mozzarella, oregano and parmesan, with warm garlic tomato dip
s.how: Heat the oven to 200C and line a tray. Roll 500g pizza dough into a 40 x 30cm rectangle. Spread with 100g tomato passata, sprinkle with 1 tsp dried oregano, 200g grated mozzarella and half of 40g grated parmesan. Roll up from the long side, cut into 12 scrolls and lay them cut side up on the tray. Brush with 1 tbsp olive oil, sprinkle with the rest of the parmesan and rest 15 minutes, then bake for 20 minutes until golden. Simmer 300g passata with 1 crushed garlic clove, 0.5 tsp chilli flakes and 0.5 tsp salt for 5 minutes and serve warm for dipping.

s.note: Thin beef strips marinated in soy, brown sugar, garlic and smoked paprika, dried low until chewy
s.how: Freeze 750g trimmed beef topside for an hour to firm up, then slice 4mm thick against the grain. Whisk 125ml soy sauce with 2 tbsp brown sugar, 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 1 tsp each of smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder and cracked black pepper and 0.5 tsp chilli flakes. Toss the beef through and marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours. Heat the oven to 75C, pat the strips dry and lay them on wire racks over trays. Dry with the door wedged slightly open for about 3.5 hours, turning once, until leathery but still bendy. Cool before packing.

m.note: Slow-simmered beef chuck chilli with chipotle, black beans and tomato, with sour cream, cheddar and corn chips
m.how: Season 1kg beef chuck in 3cm cubes with 1 tsp salt and brown in batches in 2 tbsp vegetable oil. Soften 2 diced onions and 1 diced red capsicum, then stir in 4 crushed garlic cloves, 2 chopped chipotle chillies in adobo, 2 tsp each of ground cumin and smoked paprika, 1 tsp dried oregano and 2 tbsp tomato paste. Add a 400g tin of crushed tomatoes and 500ml beef stock, return the beef, cover and simmer for 2 hours until tender. Stir in 800g drained black beans and 20g dark chocolate and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes to thicken. Serve with 150g sour cream, 100g grated cheddar, 200g corn chips and lime wedges.

w.note: Chocolate rounds, orange buttercream. Laurie lights the trap
w.how: Heat the oven to 180C and line 2 trays. Whisk 250g plain flour, 40g cocoa, 1 tsp bicarb soda and a pinch of salt. Beat 115g soft butter with 200g brown sugar until pale, then beat in 1 egg and 1 tsp vanilla. Fold in the dry mix and 250ml buttermilk alternately. Spoon 24 rounds onto the trays and bake for 12 minutes until springy, then cool. Beat 125g soft butter with 250g icing sugar, 1 tbsp milk, another 1 tsp vanilla and a little orange food colouring until fluffy, and sandwich the cakes together in pairs.

d.note: Rye, ginger beer and lime. Say something, Michael. He never does
d.how: Muddle 2 thin slices of fresh ginger with a squeeze of lime juice in each of 4 tumblers. Fill with ice, add 45ml rye whiskey to each and top with 800ml cold ginger beer. Stir and finish with a lime wedge.
